title: Sized structures and flag rules
description:
This time you are on the other side of the page: implement two functions of an imaginary system API so that they behave as their documentation (below) promises, the way lesson 3.04 describes.

**fillInfo**

```cpp-norun
struct InfoV1 { std::uint32_t cbSize; std::uint32_t processors; std::uint32_t pageSize; };
struct InfoV2 { std::uint32_t cbSize; std::uint32_t processors; std::uint32_t pageSize; std::uint32_t flags; std::uint64_t totalMemory; };

bool fillInfo(void* info);
```

`info` points to an `InfoV1` or an `InfoV2` whose `cbSize` the caller has set. The function fills in every member of that version except `cbSize`, using the constants `kProcessors`, `kPageSize`, `kFlags` and `kTotalMemory`, and returns true with `g_lastError` set to 0. It never writes beyond `cbSize` bytes. If `info` is null, or `cbSize` is not the size of one of the two structures, it returns false with `g_lastError` set to `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` and writes nothing. (The memory may not be aligned for the structure: copy bytes rather than casting the pointer.)

**checkOpenFlags** and **checkDisposition**

```cpp-norun
std::uint32_t checkOpenFlags(std::uint32_t flags);       // "one or more of the following values"
std::uint32_t checkDisposition(std::uint32_t value);     // "one of the following values"
```

`flags` combines `FLAG_READ` (0x1), `FLAG_WRITE` (0x2), `FLAG_CREATE` (0x4), `FLAG_TRUNCATE` (0x8), `FLAG_APPEND` (0x10) and `FLAG_EXCLUSIVE` (0x20). `checkOpenFlags` returns `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` if any other bit is set, if neither `FLAG_READ` nor `FLAG_WRITE` is set, if `FLAG_TRUNCATE` or `FLAG_APPEND` is set without `FLAG_WRITE`, if `FLAG_TRUNCATE` and `FLAG_APPEND` are both set, or if `FLAG_EXCLUSIVE` is set without `FLAG_CREATE`; otherwise `ERROR_SUCCESS` (0).

`checkDisposition` accepts exactly one of the values 1 to 5 (`CREATE_NEW` to `TRUNCATE_EXISTING`) and returns `ERROR_SUCCESS`; anything else gives `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`.
hints: Read `cbSize` with `std::memcpy` into a local variable, decide the version from it, build a complete local structure, and `memcpy` exactly that structure's size back. Nothing past `cbSize` can then be touched.
For the flags, test the unknown bits first with a mask of every known flag, then each documented rule in turn. Each rule is one `if`.
